Be able to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in heat transfer.
Be able to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs of thermal systems and installations that meet specific requirements.
Have an understanding of different heat transfer methods and the ability to use them.
Be able to design and conduct heat transfer experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Be able to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve heat transfer problems.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in heat transfer and their limitations.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Introduction to heat transfer by convection. 1.1 Introduction. 1.2 Boundary layers in convective processes: thermal and hydrodynamic boundary layer, laminar and turbulent flow. 1.3 Boundary layer equations. 1.4 Dimensionless equations of convective processes: Reynolds number and Nusselt number. 1.5 Turbulent boundary layers.

Topic 2. Heat transfer by convection in external flow. 2.1 Problem definition. 2.2 Determination of convective coefficients. 2.3 Case studies: flat plate (laminar and turbulent flows and critical Reynolds number), cylinder in cross flow, non-circular cylinders in cross flow, sphere, tube bank, impinging jets on a flat wall.

Topic 3. Heat transfer in internal flow. 3.1 Hydrodynamic aspects of internal flow: laminar and turbulent flow, critical Reynolds, developed and undeveloped flow, pressure drop in ducts. 3.2 Thermal aspects of internal flow. 3.3 Energy balance in ducts: case with uniform flow, case with uniform wall temperature, case with external convection; logarithmic mean temperature difference. 3.4 Correlations for internal flow.

Topic 4. Free convection heat transfer. 4.1 Introduction. 4.2 Process equations: introduction of buoyancy effect. 4.3 Dimensionless equations: Grashof and Rayleigh numbers, transition to turbulent flow on a vertical wall, heat transfer combining forced and free flow. 4.4 Free convection correlations: external flow, channels and enclosed spaces.

Topic 5. Heat transfer by phase change. 5.1 Introduction: relevant dimensionless parameters. 5.2 Heat transfer by boiling: pool boiling, forced convection boiling. 5.3 Heat transfer by condensation: film condensation on vertical surface, film condensation on horizontal tubes and spheres, film condensation on tube bundle, film condensation inside horizontal tubes, dropwise condensation on vertical surface.

Topic 6. Heat exchangers. 6.1 Types of exchangers, parallel and counter-flow. 6.2 Overall coefficient and total thermal resistance. 6.3 Calculation of exchangers: logarithmic mean temperature difference, epsilon-NTU method, P-NTU method, characteristic curves. 6.4 Shell-and-tube exchangers. 6.5 Plate exchangers. 6.6 Cross-flow heat exchangers and compact heat exchangers.

Topic 7. Psychrometry. 7.1 Atmospheric air. 7.2 Humidity measurement parameters. 7.3 Mass and energy balances, mixture enthalpy. 7.4 Saturation processes: dew point temperature, adiabatic saturation temperature, wet bulb temperature. 7.5 Psychrometric chart. 7.6 Psychrometry applications: sensible heating/cooling, humidification, evaporative cooling, dehumidification, adiabatic mixing and cooling towers.

Topic 8. Heat transfer by radiation. 8.1 Introduction to thermal radiation. 8.2 Blackbody radiation. 8.3 Radiation intensity and powers. 8.4 Radiation on real surfaces: emissivity, absorptivity, reflectivity, and transmissivity. Kirchhoff's Law. 8.5 Solar radiation. Net radiation from a surface. 8.6 Radiation between surfaces: view factors, net heat exchange by radiation between black surfaces and between gray and diffuse surfaces, thermal radiation circuits, application examples (radiation shields, re-radiating surfaces) and combined heat transfer.
assessment_rules: Continuous assessment is conducted throughout the course through partial exams and laboratory practices. The final exam focuses on solving practical problems. A minimum score of 4 in the final exam is required to pass the course.
